- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly, especially if recent prices are falling.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model often overcorrects in next period; dampen forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; align forecast with sentiment shift direction.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–2% per day.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish; adjust downward by 1–2% for first 7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” (neutral), model often drifts toward overestimation; apply a 0.5–1% downward bias to avoid false momentum.
